2.1 Purpose

This Project Charter defines the organizational structure, governance framework, site details, and baseline asset information for the Renewable Energy Maintenance Consortium (REMC). - Understanding of protection and control systems, including overcurrent, earth fault, and differential protection.

**6. SITE-SPECIFIC TECHNICAL DATA**

**6.1 Port Harcourt Hybrid Plant – Overview**

The Port Harcourt Hybrid Plant is located in the Trans-Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State. The site combines solar PV generation with battery storage and a standby diesel generator to provide firm power to the local distribution network. The plant operates in both grid-connected and islanded modes, depending on grid conditions and dispatch instructions.

**6.1.1 Solar PV Arrays**

- **North Block:** 12 MWp capacity, comprising 32,000 monocrystalline modules mounted on fixed-tilt structures. The array is divided into 12 inverters units, each rated at 1 MW.  
- **South Block:** 8 MWp capacity, comprising 21,500 modules on single-axis trackers. The tracking system is designed to optimise yield during the dry season.

**6.1.2 Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)**

The BESS provides 10 MW / 20 MWh of storage capacity, using lithium-ion cells arranged in 40 containerised units. The system supports grid stabilisation, peak shaving, and black-start capability. The BESS is controlled by the site SCADA system and is capable of responding to frequency regulation signals within 200 ms.

**6.1.3 Diesel Generator**

A 2 MW standby diesel generator is installed to provide backup power during extended grid outages or when solar and battery resources are insufficient. The generator is tested under load on a monthly basis and is maintained in accordance with the manufacturer’s schedule.

**6.2 Grid Connection**

The plant is connected to the 132 kV transmission network via a dedicated 8 km overhead line to the Rumuola 132 kV substation, owned by the Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Company (PHEDC). The connection is covered by the Grid Connection Agreement (REMC-GCA-PHH-001) and is subject to the Nigerian Grid Code. The plant operates under a PHEDC dispatch instruction regime and is required to provide reactive power within a power factor range of 0.95 leading to 0.95 lagging at the point of interconnection.
**7. OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE FRAMEWORK**

**7.1 Maintenance Strategy**

REMC operates a preventive and predictive maintenance programme across all sites, supplemented by corrective maintenance for emergent faults. The maintenance strategy is aligned with the manufacturer’s recommendations and the requirements of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC). All maintenance activities are planned on a 12-month rolling schedule, reviewed quarterly by the Site Operations Manager and the Head of Engineering.

The maintenance year is defined as 1 January to 31 December. The annual maintenance plan is issued no later than 30 November of the preceding year. Changes to the plan are managed through the Maintenance Change Request process (MCR), which requires approval from the Head of Engineering and notification to the relevant Distribution Company (DisCo) where grid availability may be affected.

**7.2 Maintenance Categories**

Maintenance activities are classified into the following categories:

| Category | Description | Typical Frequency |
|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| Routine | Visual inspections, cleaning, thermal scanning of electrical connections, functional checks | Monthly |
| Periodic | Lubrication, torque checks, calibration of protection relays, insulation resistance testing | Quarterly to annually |
| Predictive | Oil analysis, vibration analysis, thermography, battery capacity testing | Per condition-based schedule |
| Corrective | Repair or replacement of failed components | As required |
| Major Overhaul | Comprehensive refurbishment of major plant items, e.g. inverters, transformers, diesel generator | Per manufacturer’s schedule |

All maintenance work is recorded in the Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Work orders are raised for all activities, including routine inspections. Each work order is assigned a unique identifier with the prefix WO, followed by the site code and a sequential number. For example, WO-PHH-2023-0142 refers to the 142nd work order raised at the Port Harcourt Hybrid Plant in 2023.

**7.3 Safety Standards**

All maintenance activities are undertaken in accordance with the REMC Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Policy and the provisions of the Nigerian Labour Act. The following safety standards apply:

- **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Mandatory for all work on electrical equipment, including inverters, switchgear, and the BESS. LOTO procedures are verified by a second competent person before work commences.
- **Permit to Work (PTW):** Required for all high-risk activities, including working at height, confined space entry, live electrical work, and lifting operations. PTWs are issued by the Site HSE Officer and are valid for a single shift unless extended in writing.
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** Minimum PPE for all site personnel is a hard hat, safety boots, high-visibility vest, and safety glasses. Additional PPE, such as arc-flash rated clothing, is required for specific tasks.
- **Arc Flash Study:** An arc flash study has been completed for all sites. The study results are displayed on equipment labels and are used to determine approach distances and required PPE.

**7.4 Reporting Protocols**

The following reporting protocols apply to all sites:

- **Daily Operations Report:** Submitted by the Shift Supervisor to the Site Operations Manager by 08:00 each day. The report covers generation output, grid availability, plant status, and any incidents or near misses.
- **Weekly Maintenance Report:** Submitted by the Maintenance Supervisor to the Head of Engineering every Friday. The report summarises completed work orders, pending work, and any equipment performance issues.
- **Monthly Performance Report:** Submitted by the Site Operations Manager to the Managing Director and the Board by the 5th working day of the following month. The report includes availability, energy yield, forced outage hours, and maintenance backlog.
- **Incident Report:** Any safety incident, environmental incident, or significant equipment failure is reported verbally to the Site Operations Manager and the Head of Engineering within 1 hour of occurrence. A written Incident Report is submitted within 24 hours using the standard template.

**8.1 Purpose of the Role**

The Maintenance Technician position exists to support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of REMC’s generation and distribution assets. Technicians perform routine inspections, preventive maintenance, fault diagnosis, and corrective repairs across all sites, working under the direction of the Site Maintenance Supervisor and with support from the Head of Engineering Services.

The role is field-based and requires regular travel between sites, including overnight stays where operational needs dictate. Technicians are expected to work shift patterns, including weekends and public holidays, to ensure continuity of service. **8.3 Core Responsibilities**

The Maintenance Technician is responsible for the following duties, which are not exhaustive and may be adjusted by the Head of Engineering Services to meet operational requirements:

- Performing scheduled preventive maintenance tasks on diesel generators, transformers, switchgear, and auxiliary plant in accordance with the approved maintenance schedule.
- Conducting routine visual inspections of equipment, identifying signs of wear, leakage, corrosion, overheating, or vibration, and reporting findings through the work order system.
- Diagnosing faults and carrying out corrective repairs, including replacement of components, recalibration of protection relays, and re-torquing of connections.
- Operating and maintaining the site’s SCADA and monitoring systems as required, including taking readings and logging operational parameters.
- Responding to plant alarms and operational emergencies, including out-of-hours call-outs, and taking appropriate action to protect personnel and equipment.
- Assisting in the execution of the annual overhaul programme for major generating units, including preparation of tools, materials, and isolation certificates.
- Maintaining accurate maintenance records, including work orders, inspection sheets, and equipment history logs, and ensuring that all documentation is completed within the same shift.
- Ensuring that all work is carried out in compliance with the REMC Safety Management System, Permit-to-Work procedures, and lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) requirements.
- Participating in toolbox talks, safety briefings, and emergency response drills as scheduled.
- Ordering spare parts and consumables through the approved procurement process, and verifying that received goods match the order specification.
- Training and mentoring junior technicians and apprentices as assigned by the Site Maintenance Supervisor.
- Performing housekeeping duties to maintain a clean, organised, and safe working environment in workshops, stores, and plant rooms.

- Practical knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems used in power generation, including diesel engines, alternators, excitation systems, and cooling systems.
- Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, mechanical drawings, and manufacturer manuals.
- Proficiency in the use of test instruments, including multimeters, insulation testers, thermal imaging cameras, and vibration analysers.
- Familiarity with predictive maintenance techniques, including oil analysis and thermography.
- Understanding of protection and control systems, including overcurrent, earth fault, and differential protection.
- Working knowledge of Nigerian grid code requirements as they relate to plant operation and maintenance.
- Basic computer literacy, including the use of email, word processing, and the CMMS (Computerised Maintenance Management System).

**7. OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE FRAMEWORK**

**7.1 Maintenance Strategy**

REMC operates a preventive and predictive maintenance programme across all sites, supplemented by corrective maintenance for emergent faults. The maintenance strategy is aligned with the manufacturer’s recommendations and the requirements of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC). All maintenance activities are planned on a 12-month rolling schedule, reviewed quarterly by the Site Operations Manager and the Head of Engineering.

The maintenance year is defined as 1 January to 31 December. The annual maintenance plan is issued no later than 30 November of the preceding year. Changes to the plan are managed through the Maintenance Change Request process (MCR), which requires approval from the Head of Engineering and notification to the relevant Distribution Company (DisCo) where grid availability may be affected.

**7.2 Maintenance Categories**

Maintenance activities are classified into the following categories:

| Category | Description | Typical Frequency |
|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| Routine | Visual inspections, cleaning, thermal scanning of electrical connections, functional checks | Monthly |
| Periodic | Lubrication, torque checks, calibration of protection relays, insulation resistance testing | Quarterly to annually |
| Predictive | Oil analysis, vibration analysis, thermography, battery capacity testing | Per condition-based schedule |
| Corrective | Repair or replacement of failed components | As required |
| Major Overhaul | Comprehensive refurbishment of major plant items, e.g. inverters, transformers, diesel generator | Per manufacturer’s schedule |

All maintenance work is recorded in the Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Work orders are raised for all activities, including routine inspections. Each work order is assigned a unique identifier with the prefix WO, followed by the site code and a sequential number. For example, WO-PHH-2023-0142 refers to the 142nd work order raised at the Port Harcourt Hybrid Plant in 2023.

**7.3 Safety Standards**

All maintenance activities are undertaken in accordance with the REMC Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Policy and the provisions of the Nigerian Labour Act. The following safety standards apply:

- **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Mandatory for all work on electrical equipment, including inverters, switchgear, and the BESS. LOTO procedures are verified by a second competent person before work commences.
- **Permit to Work (PTW):** Required for all high-risk activities, including working at height, confined space entry, live electrical work, and lifting operations. PTWs are issued by the Site HSE Officer and are valid for a single shift unless extended in writing.
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** Minimum PPE for all site personnel is a hard hat, safety boots, high-visibility vest, and safety glasses. Additional PPE, such as arc-flash rated clothing, is required for specific tasks.
- **Arc Flash Study:** An arc flash study has been completed for all sites. The study results are displayed on equipment labels and are used to determine approach distances and required PPE.

**7.4 Reporting Protocols**

The following reporting protocols apply to all sites:

- **Daily Operations Report:** Submitted by the Shift Supervisor to the Site Operations Manager by 08:00 each day. The report covers generation output, grid availability, plant status, and any incidents or near misses.
- **Weekly Maintenance Report:** Submitted by the Maintenance Supervisor to the Head of Engineering every Friday. The report summarises completed work orders, pending work, and any equipment performance issues.
- **Monthly Performance Report:** Submitted by the Site Operations Manager to the Managing Director and the Board by the 5th working day of the following month. The report includes availability, energy yield, forced outage hours, and maintenance backlog.
- **Incident Report:** Any safety incident, environmental incident, or significant equipment failure is reported verbally to the Site Operations Manager and the Head of Engineering within 1 hour of occurrence. A written Incident Report is submitted within 24 hours using the standard template.
